name: Browser state security
description: Validate browser state save/load while treating serialized state as a credential.

variants.description: Capture and replay an expiring fake session against a local authentication fixture.
setup: Start a local auth fixture that issues a nonce-scoped, short-lived cookie and storage record with no real account value.
Create a permission-restricted temporary directory for the serialized browser state.
exercise: Authenticate to the local fixture, save state, close the first browser, load state into a fresh browser, and navigate to the protected route.
After the positive replay, expire the fixture session and prove stale state is rejected.

assertions.expectation: The state file is created only inside the restricted run directory and is never printed or embedded in reports.
A fresh browser reaches the protected nonce-tagged route without a second login after loading valid state.
Expired state is rejected and does not silently grant access.
All browsers, state files, cookies, storage, and fixture processes are removed.

cleanup: Clear browser storage, close owned surfaces, and stop the local auth server.
Securely remove the run-owned state fixture using the platform's normal deletion semantics and discard its session server state.

variants.description: Manually verify state replay for an explicitly authorized real account in a dedicated profile.
setup: Use a dedicated Cmux/browser profile and a least-privilege test account approved for session replay.
Choose a permission-restricted state path with a documented retention deadline and disable evidence capture of credential contents.
exercise: Have the authorized human complete login, save state, close the source browser, load state into one fresh owned browser, and open a read-only account page.
Do not perform writes, purchases, messages, permission changes, or any other account mutation.

assertions.expectation: The account, target service, allowed page, and state-retention window were explicitly authorized before capture.
The fresh browser reaches only the approved read-only page without reauthentication.
No cookie, token, local-storage value, or state-file content appears in logs, screenshots, diffs, or reports.
The state file, profile, and server-side test session are deleted or revoked at the agreed deadline.

cleanup: Close all owned browser surfaces and delete the serialized state from the dedicated profile.
Revoke the test session where supported, discard the profile, and retain only a non-sensitive pass/fail record.
